title: Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Really Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling?
abstract: arXiv:2608.19833v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Sequential recommenders increasingly use language-model architectures designed to capture complex, context-dependent interactions. Yet it remains unclear whether widely used benchmarks actually require this modelling capacity. We investigate this question using two simple, recency-weighted pairwise probes that do not learn higher-order sequence representations: Sequential Rules (SeqRules) and our Probabilistic Collaborative Transition Model (PCTM). Using the evaluation protocol of eSASRec, at least one probe exceeds our eSASRec reproduction by 15-38% on three Amazon datasets and by 4.4% on MovieLens-1M, but trails it by 27.3% on MovieLens-20M. On the four remaining datasets, at least one probe also outperforms our sampled-softmax SASRec reproduction by 9-28%, suggesting that these widely used benchmarks are poorly suited to measuring gains from higher-order sequence modelling. translated_title: 顺序推荐基准测试真的需要高阶序列建模吗？
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.19833v1 公告类型：新 摘要：顺序推荐器越来越多地使用旨在捕获复杂、上下文依赖交互的语言模型架构。然而，目前尚不清楚广泛使用的基准测试是否真正需要这种建模能力。我们通过两个简单的、基于近期加权的成对探针来研究这个问题，这些探针不学习高阶序列表示：顺序规则（SeqRules）和我们的概率协作转移模型（PCM）。使用eSASRec的评估协议，至少一个探针在三个Amazon数据集上超过我们的eSASRec复现结果15-38%，在MovieLens-1M上超过4.4%，但在MovieLens-20M上落后27.3%。在其余四个数据集上，至少一个探针也优于我们的采样softmax SASRec复现结果9-28%，这表明这些广泛使用的基准测试不适合衡量高阶序列建模带来的收益。更广泛地说，将基于Transformer的模型与强基线进行比较时，需要谨慎。
tldr: 本文通过两个简单探针证明，广泛使用的顺序推荐基准测试可能无法有效区分高阶序列建模带来的收益，提示现有评估协议存在局限性。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that widely used sequential recommendation benchmarks may fail to effectively measure gains from higher-order sequence modeling, using two simple probes that outperform strong baselines on most datasets.
